title: The repair estimate is bigger than expected
prompt: Your transport needs a $1,600 repair or replacement arrangement. The normal budget includes a routine repairs allowance, but this is an additional failure. You need reliable travel for work.
context: All prices are scenario amounts. Financing here creates consumer debt at the model rate.

choices.label: Pay the full repair
choices.text: Spend $1,600 and keep the current travel arrangement.
choices.feedback: Travel is restored. The repair takes a large part of a small emergency buffer.

choices.label: Finance the repair
choices.text: Add $1,600 consumer debt; keep cash available.
choices.feedback: The bill has not disappeared. Consumer interest and scheduled payments now enter later budgets.

choices.label: Arrange a temporary workaround
choices.text: Spend $350 now and defer the unresolved problem.
choices.feedback: You gain time rather than a permanent fix. A later transport decision will return to the problem.

title: The temporary repair was only temporary
prompt: The transport problem you deferred is now harder to manage. A permanent solution costs $2,100. The workaround is still consuming time and may disrupt work.
context: Your earlier decision kept cash available but did not remove this obligation.

choices.label: Fix it now
choices.text: Pay $2,100 and end the workaround.
choices.feedback: You resolve the problem at a higher cost than the earlier estimate.

choices.label: Borrow for the permanent fix
choices.text: Add $2,100 consumer debt and restore the usual commute.
choices.feedback: The problem is resolved, but the financing cost continues through the debt model.

choices.label: Continue the workaround
choices.text: Spend another $450 and lose $800 gross from missed work.
choices.feedback: The stopgap now costs both money and pay. The unresolved flag remains for a later year.

title: Your lease renewal
prompt: The housing-cost increase is larger than the normal model inflation already in your budget. You can accept an additional $120 monthly charge or spend money to find an alternative.
context: The additional charge starts this year and recurs; normal annual inflation still applies.

choices.label: Accept the renewal
choices.text: Add $120/month to housing costs from now on.
choices.feedback: You avoid moving costs while accepting an ongoing increase.

choices.label: Move to another suitable place
choices.text: Spend $1,800 on moving costs and nonrefundable fees; avoid the extra charge.
choices.feedback: The new place avoids the extra increase. Moving still requires cash and substantial effort.

choices.label: Negotiate a smaller increase
choices.text: Spend time comparing alternatives; accept an extra $60/month.
choices.feedback: In this story the landlord accepts the smaller increase. Negotiation cannot be assumed to work in every real case.

title: A dental bill outside the routine budget
prompt: A necessary dental procedure leaves $1,100 out of pocket after the fictional insurance benefit. Routine medical costs in the budget do not cover this additional bill.
context: The payment arrangement below is a specific scenario offer, not a universal medical policy.

choices.label: Pay the bill
choices.text: Use $1,100 cash.
choices.feedback: You resolve the bill and reduce the cash available for the next unexpected cost.

choices.label: Use the offered staged plan
choices.text: Pay $500 now and $50/month for the next year.
choices.feedback: You keep more cash now. The monthly commitment stays until the follow-up ends it.

choices.label: Use consumer credit
choices.text: Add $1,100 consumer debt.
choices.feedback: Treatment is not delayed. Consumer interest makes carrying the balance costly.

title: The dental payment plan ends
prompt: The staged dental plan has reached its final scheduled year. The $50 monthly payment can now come out of your regular budget. You also have other uses for that money.
context: This follow-up removes the recurring cost introduced by your earlier choice.

choices.label: Return the payment to your buffer
choices.text: Remove the $50 monthly charge.
choices.feedback: Your normal budget improves. Savings appear through lower bills rather than an invented cash reward.

choices.label: Keep part for routine care
choices.text: Reduce the monthly charge by $25 and keep $25 for care.
choices.feedback: You improve cash flow and keep a little more room for ongoing health needs.

choices.label: Redirect it to family support
choices.text: Remove the $50 medical charge; add $50/month to family support.
choices.feedback: Your total commitment stays similar, but its purpose changes.

title: Find room in the everyday budget
prompt: Your food, household, and social budget is difficult to sustain. You can make recurring cuts, but each option changes how you spend time or connect with people.
context: Savings reduce actual modeled categories; they are not free cash awards.

choices.label: Plan meals and reduce convenience spending
choices.text: Cut groceries by $60/month; spend more time planning.
choices.feedback: The lower grocery budget helps each year. Planning and preparation take time.

choices.label: Reduce paid outings
choices.text: Cut social spending by $80/month and arrange lower-cost meetups.
choices.feedback: Spending falls while maintaining connections takes a little more effort.

choices.label: Keep the current routine
choices.text: Make no category cuts this year.
choices.feedback: Convenience and familiar activities remain, along with the full bill.

title: A replacement phone is needed
prompt: Your phone fails and is required for daily communication. Repair is no longer practical. You can replace it at different costs; the current phone/internet bill is already budgeted.
context: A device installment is an additional recurring obligation, not a reduction in your normal bill.

choices.label: Buy a basic refurbished replacement
choices.text: Spend $280 cash.
choices.feedback: You restore the essential function without the premium features.

choices.label: Buy a new premium device
choices.text: Spend $1,100 cash.
choices.feedback: You enjoy the device while giving up a much larger amount of cash.

choices.label: Choose a two-year installment offer
choices.text: Add $35/month to the phone category.
choices.feedback: The upfront price is lower. This recurring bill continues until its follow-up ends it.

title: Your device installment is paid off
prompt: The two-year phone installment is complete. Its $35 monthly charge can end. You can keep the working device or choose another upgrade.
context: The follow-up ends the earlier installment before any new purchase is added.

choices.label: Keep the working device
choices.text: Remove $35/month from the phone bill.
choices.feedback: Keeping the device creates recurring room in your budget.

choices.label: Replace the battery and keep it
choices.text: Spend $90 and remove $35/month.
choices.feedback: A smaller maintenance cost can extend the life of something you already own.

choices.label: Start a new installment
choices.text: Keep the same $35 monthly charge for another device.
choices.feedback: The old agreement ends, but a new ongoing charge takes its place. The model keeps that charge beyond this year.

title: Insurance costs more this year
prompt: The fictional plan premium increases beyond the normal inflation already modeled. You can keep the plan or switch to a cheaper plan with a higher out-of-pocket burden.
context: The cheaper premium is paired with a modeled increase in routine medical costs.

choices.label: Keep the current plan
choices.text: Add $65/month to health premiums.
choices.feedback: Predictable coverage costs more each month.

choices.label: Choose the lower-premium plan
choices.text: Add $15/month to premiums and $45/month to expected medical spending.
choices.feedback: The premium looks cheaper, but much of the difference moves to out-of-pocket spending.

choices.label: Use a narrower provider network
choices.text: Add $30/month to premiums and $20/month to travel costs.
choices.feedback: You trade provider convenience and travel time for a lower premium increase.

title: Debt payment or a cash buffer?
prompt: You can choose whether to use up to $1,000 of cash toward debt. Required yearly payments will still be settled later. A small buffer may matter when the next bill arrives.
context: Extra payments are capped by cash and the remaining debt; consumer debt is paid first.

choices.label: Pay extra toward debt
choices.text: Use up to $1,000 available cash.
choices.feedback: The actual payment reduces debt and cash together. You have less cash available for an emergency.

choices.label: Keep the buffer
choices.text: Leave cash available and make only scheduled payments.
choices.feedback: Liquidity stays available. Debt interest continues to accrue.

choices.label: Spend on a short break
choices.text: Spend $550 for time away.
choices.feedback: Recovery matters, and it comes with an opportunity cost in your budget.

title: A household essential breaks
prompt: An essential appliance or household item fails. You are responsible for replacement in this scenario. The normal maintenance budget does not cover the whole additional cost.
context: Sharing a household can distribute responsibility, but does not make every bill disappear.

choices.label: Buy a reliable replacement
choices.text: Spend $750 cash.
choices.feedback: The problem is resolved and your reserve is smaller.

choices.label: Choose a used replacement
choices.text: Spend $300 and accept more uncertainty about lifespan.
choices.feedback: The lower price preserves cash while leaving more uncertainty.

choices.label: Use consumer financing
choices.text: Add $750 consumer debt.
choices.feedback: The item is replaced. Carrying the cost forward adds interest and future payments.

title: An application fee you did not plan for
prompt: A housing, credential, or administrative renewal costs $420 in this story. The deadline is approaching. A late extension adds a fee, so delaying is not free.
context: This is an illustrative administrative cost, not a statement of a particular licensing fee.

choices.label: Pay on time
choices.text: Spend $420.
choices.feedback: You avoid penalties, while the cost still reduces your buffer.

choices.label: Take a short extension
choices.text: Spend $170 now and add $300 consumer debt for the remaining cost and fee.
choices.feedback: The extension creates time at a higher total cost.

choices.label: Reduce other spending to offset it
choices.text: Pay $420; cut social spending by $25/month going forward.
choices.feedback: The initial bill remains. A lasting budget cut helps absorb similar costs later.
